name: Security baseline
summary: App-security guardrails every repo should meet — secrets, logging, input, authz.

name: TDD discipline
summary: Test-first discipline: a failing test before code, green before merge, real assertions.

name: Rust conventions
summary: Idiomatic, panic-averse Rust: propagate errors, clippy-clean, fail closed on safety.

name: TypeScript + Svelte conventions
summary: Strict TS + Svelte 5 house style: no any, no default exports, server state via the query layer, a11y.

name: Sensei field notes
source: sensei — observed over real AI-assisted work
summary: Hard-won lessons sensei learned in the field: verify against reality, keep the human in the loop, small safe steps.

name: Clean Code guidelines
summary: Readable, intention-revealing code: good names, small single-purpose functions, no hidden side effects, DRY, comments that explain why.

name: Design principles (SOLID)
summary: Sound module design: single responsibility, depend on abstractions, open/closed, composition over inheritance, YAGNI.

name: Compliance baseline
summary: Regulated-data guardrails: minimize, get lawful basis, encrypt, audit access, honor data-subject rights.

name: UX & design principles
summary: Usable, accessible interfaces: a11y first, clear feedback, recoverable errors, consistency, respect the user's time.

name: Default constitution — architecture guardrails
source: sensei default constitution (DORA · XP/CD · Core Protocols)
summary: Design + pattern guardrails: the simplest design that passes the tests, continuous refactor, small single-purpose changes, match the house style, and reuse before a 4th near-duplicate.

name: Default constitution — principles
source: sensei default constitution (DORA · XP/CD · Core Protocols)
summary: The mandatory principles every sensei ships knowing: measure and keep what helps, direction over raw speed, strong fundamentals first, and make it safe to question the AI.

name: Default constitution — process guardrails
source: sensei default constitution (DORA · XP/CD · Core Protocols)
summary: Quality, flow, tooling and practice guardrails: a test with every change, never merge on red, human review of AI code, trunk-based flow, short lead time, a green pipeline, and a sustainable pace.

name: Ponytail — minimal-solution discipline
summary: The laziest solution that actually works: don't write what you don't need, reuse before you build, prefer the platform over a dependency, keep the diff minimal.

name: Stack templates — opt-in per stack
summary: Opt-in, per-stack coding templates (Rust · TypeScript/Svelte · Python) a project adopts when the stack matches — seeded but not auto-adopted.
